title: Maximum Difference Between Increasing Elements
statement:
You are given an integer array `nums` of length `n`. Over all index pairs `i` and `j` with `0 <= i < j < n` where the later value is strictly larger (`nums[i] < nums[j]`), find the largest value of `nums[j] - nums[i]` and return it.

If no pair satisfies both conditions, return `-1`.
notes:
## Intuition

Checking every pair `i < j` takes O(n²). For a fixed later index `j`, though, the best partner is simply the smallest value seen before it. So walk once from left to right, remembering the running minimum, and treat each new value as a possible right end of the pair.

## Approach

1. Set `smallest` to `nums[0]` and `best` to `-1` (no valid pair yet).
2. For each `j` from 1 onward, if `nums[j]` is strictly greater than `smallest`, the pair is valid: update `best` with `nums[j] - smallest`.
3. Otherwise `nums[j]` is a new minimum (or ties it), so store it in `smallest`.
4. Return `best`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [7, 1, 5, 4]`. Start with `smallest = 7`, `best = -1`. At `j = 1`, `1` is not larger than `7`, so `smallest = 1`. At `j = 2`, `5 > 1`, so `best = 5 - 1 = 4`. At `j = 3`, `4 > 1` gives `3`, which does not beat `4`. The answer is `4`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass over the array.
- Space: O(1): two numbers.

## Pitfalls

- The pair needs a strict increase; equal values give a difference of `0` that does not count, so an all-equal array returns `-1`, not `0`.
- The smaller value must come first; the overall minimum and maximum may be in the wrong order (Example 1).
- Starting `best` at `0` would wrongly return `0` when no pair exists.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `smallest` | smallest value among `nums[0..j-1]` |
| `best` | largest valid difference so far, or `-1` |
| `j` | index of the possible right end of a pair |

narration.2: The first value is the only candidate for the smaller end so far.
narration.3: -1 means no valid pair has been found yet.
narration.4: Try each later index j as the larger end of a pair.
narration.5: A strictly larger value than the running minimum forms a valid pair.
narration.6: Keep the biggest difference found so far.
narration.8: Otherwise this value is no larger than the minimum, so it becomes the new minimum.
narration.11: Return the best difference, or -1 if no pair was valid.
